entry.title: No. 9: A guard for f6
entry.summary: Thirteen units, no flight. A white pawn stands on e7 between the bishop on d8 and the black pawn on f6. Promoting it opens the bishop's diagonal. Then ask which of the four new pieces can protect the square the bishop lands on.

entry.title: No. 8: Checks from a pinned knight
entry.summary: Seventeen units, no flight. The white king stands in front of its own rook on the fourth rank, and only a black knight on d4 keeps that battery closed. Two of the knight's captures give check and pin the knight at the same moment. Look at what a pinned knight can still do, and what it can no longer do.

entry.title: No. 7: Two on the long diagonal
entry.summary: Fourteen units, no flight. The bishop in the corner looks through a black rook and a black knight at the king. Neither is pinned yet, but as soon as one of them moves, the other is. White's quiet first move gives the king a square.

entry.title: No. 6: A crossing on e7
entry.summary: Fifteen units, no flight. The queen's best mate is on f6, and her own rook stands there. The rook has only one way to step aside. After that, the black rook and the black bishop both want e7, and each gets in the other's way.

entry.title: No. 5: Three guards for e6
entry.summary: Sixteen units, no flight in the diagram. The queen has a line to e6, but her own knight stands in the way. Clearing it is not enough: find the one knight move that also makes e6 safe. Then each Black defence of e6 has to stand next to its own king.

entry.title: No. 4: Study: a flight out of a pin
entry.summary: A study post: today's own attempt did not pass the gate, so here is a problem that does what it tried to do. Eleven units, no flight in the diagram. The black knight on d5 is pinned and cannot move. Find the quiet first move that sets it free and gives the king a square, then watch every knight move get its own mate.

entry.title: No. 3: Two captures on e5
entry.summary: Twelve units, no flight. Black has two ways to take the e5 pawn, and both already have a mate in the diagram. Find the quiet first move after which both captures are answered again, by different mates.

entry.title: No. 2: The diagonal that keeps e3
entry.summary: Eight units and a quiet first move. Almost every move of the black bishop loses to the same mate; two of them stop it and pay for it differently. Look at where the bishop's random moves all land.

entry.title: No. 1: The pawn that says no, then yes
entry.summary: Nine units. The obvious knight move that prepares Qd3 fails to one pawn move. Find the move after which that same pawn move loses at once.
